speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The severity of the night sweats is significant. Given the combination of B-symptoms, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and abdominal findings, I need to visualize the lymph nodes and abdominal organs more closely. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis. Do you have any history of recent infections or travel to endemic areas for parasitic diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of painless, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, abdominal pain, and significant B-symptoms (night sweats, weight loss) in the context of recent swelling progression is highly characteristic. While infectious etiologies must be ruled out, the "fixed" nature of the nodes strongly suggests malignancy. I will await your CT and lab results to confirm the staging and histology.
